title: Apply DB2_POOL_SIZE + --fail-ratio consistently to BM-14a/b/c in the locust-scale job
summary: BM-14a/b/c run 200/50/50 VUs against the SDK's default pool size of 5 with no DB2_POOL_SIZE override and no failure-rate tolerance, so any pool contention hard-fails the step even though the same workflow file already has the correct pattern elsewhere.
description:
In `.github/workflows/benchmark-suite.yml`, the `locust-scale` job's BM-14 steps (lines 403-429 — "BM-14a — UserRampUser (200 VUs, 2/s ramp, 5 min)", "BM-14b — AgentSweepUser", "BM-14c — MixedReadWriteUser") set no `DB2_POOL_SIZE` env var, so `src/agent_memory_sdk/db/connection.py`'s `_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE = 5` applies. BM-14a then drives 200 concurrent Locust users against 5 Db2 connections with no `--fail-ratio` flag, so Locust's default headless behavior (exit 1 on any request failure) applies.

Observed failure (https://github.com/priyanshu-krishnan1/yaadien/actions/runs/31242532940/job/93077463451, step "BM-14a — UserRampUser"): `ConnectionPoolExhausted('No free Db2 connection available after 30s. Pool size is 5.')`, 25 write + 20 search failures out of ~44,308 total requests (a 0.10% failure rate) — the step still exits 1 and fails the job.

The correct pattern already exists twice in this same repo: (a) every BM-15 step in the very same job (lines 431-479) explicitly sets `DB2_POOL_SIZE`; (b) the Tier 2 nightly job's own BM-14 step ("BM-14 Locust ramp — MixedReadWriteUser", ~line 588) sets both `DB2_POOL_SIZE: "20"` and `--fail-ratio 0.01`. BM-14a/b/c in the `locust-scale` job were just never brought in line with either.

Decide and implement one of:
1. Set an explicit, realistic `DB2_POOL_SIZE` (e.g. `"20"`, matching the Tier 2 precedent and BM-15's top tier) for BM-14a/b/c, plus a `--fail-ratio` threshold appropriate to a load test (e.g. `0.01`–`0.05`) so transient pool contention at high VU counts is recorded as a data point, not treated as a build break.
2. If BM-14a is deliberately meant to characterize behavior at the *default* pool size under load (i.e. pool exhaustion is the expected/interesting result), keep `DB2_POOL_SIZE` unset but add `--fail-ratio` so the step only fails on a real regression (e.g. failure rate jumping from ~0.1% to double digits), not on any nonzero exhaustion count.

Either way, the current state (oversubscribed pool, zero tolerance) is neither: it just fails deterministically without producing a usable signal on either side of that decision.

Acceptance: BM-14a/b/c complete without hard-failing under normal conditions; the workflow run's Job Summary or CSV output clearly shows the pool-exhaustion rate for BM-14a so it's visible as a metric, not just a pass/fail; a documented rationale (comment in the workflow file) explains which of the two options was chosen and why.
